display.purpose: The single page headline, message-matched to the ad that delivered the visitor. One per page.

headline.purpose: Section headings. They carry the section alone; nothing sits above them.

label.purpose: Form labels and small emphasis. Sentence case, not caps.

film-title.purpose: Social layer only. All-caps over footage, auto-shrunk to fit, ends in a full stop.

shadows.name: type-shadow
shadows.purpose: Under white type on footage, so it survives a bright frame. Social layer, always present.

shadows.name: form-lift
shadows.purpose: The form card only. Navy-tinted, so the conversion element reads as the nearest object.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Figures and cards on pointer devices only. Disabled under hover:none.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for colour and transform state changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one thing to press. Brand blue with an ink label; on trades pages it is a tel: link carrying the number as its label.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The secondary path in a hero, over a dark ground. One per view, never more.

components.name: Sticky Call Bar
components.description: Phone-first pages keep the number under the thumb. Fixed to the bottom below 820px; the page reserves calc(bar + safe-area) of bottom padding so it never covers content.

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Always labelled, never placeholder-only. Border dark enough to clear 3:1 against white and against any card tint it sits on. 16px minimum so iOS does not zoom on focus.

components.name: Conversion Form Card
components.description: The page's purpose. Four required fields maximum, one optional note, honeypot kept, positioned last on the page and framed as a callback request.
components.html: Urgent? Call 0427 593 990 instead.

components.name: Ad Page Header
components.description: There is no navigation. An unlinked wordmark and the phone number, nothing else, because every nav item is a way to lose a click you paid for.

components.name: Work Figure
components.description: Real project photography with a caption that names the project. Charcoal ground behind the image so a loading frame is not a white hole; caption coloured for that dark ground, not for white.

components.name: Licence Strip
components.description: Trades pages earn legitimacy in one second: licence numbers immediately below the hero, accent-coloured numerals on a dark band.
components.html: QLD Electrical 87592NSW Contractor 483405CFully insured, compliance certificate on every job

narrative.northStar: The Film House and the Front Door
narrative.overview: 10x Visuals designs on two surface classes that must never borrow each other's grammar. The social layer is a film house: real footage, quiet tracked type, film-title full stops, and nothing else. Restraint is the proof of premium; the less graphic design on the grid, the more it reads as work worth paying for. The web layer is a front door. These are Google and Meta ad landing pages built for clients, and their job is not admiration but a phone call. Restraint is spent differently here: one message-matched headline, an exit ramp to the phone at every scroll depth, and a short form that asks for nothing it doesn't need. The layers share type, blue and voice. They share nothing structurally.
keyCharacteristics: Photography and footage carry the design; type is the quiet layer over it
One accent blue, spent on actions, never on a surface
Landing pages are phone-first, nav-free, and end in a short form
Copy is blokey-Australian, plain, and free of dashes
Every number on a client page is verified before it ships

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The accent points at actions and nothing else. It fills buttons, marks the offer phrase, and underlines a live link. It is never a section background, never a large fill, and never two blues on one surface.

rules.name: The Surface-Not-Token Rule
rules.body: Contrast is checked against the surface a token actually lands on, not the one it was designed for. Muted grey was simultaneously compliant on white and failing on both the tinted section and the dark image figure. When a token changes, re-measure every surface it touches.

rules.name: The Not-Ours-To-Set Rule
rules.body: Client palettes are not owned here. MVX volt green, CVA monochrome, and every future client's colours live on that client's page and wiki entry. Never port one client's palette onto another's page.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: On the social layer a tracked uppercase kicker is a named brand system with a fixed vocabulary. On the web layer it is banned as section scaffolding. A kicker above every section is not voice, it is grammar borrowed from a template.

rules.name: The No-Numbers Rule
rules.body: Numbered section markers earn their place only when the section genuinely is an ordered sequence the reader must follow.

rules.name: The No-Dashes Rule
rules.body: No em dashes or en dashes anywhere in user-facing copy, on either layer.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: text-wrap: balance on headings, pretty on prose. If headline copy overflows at any breakpoint, rewrite the copy rather than reduce the scale.

rules.name: The One-Exit Rule
rules.body: An ad landing page has exactly one exit and it is the conversion. No navigation, no menu, no linked logo.

rules.name: The Thumb-Reach Rule
rules.body: On a phone-first page the number lives under the thumb, with page bottom padding computed as calc(bar-height + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)).

rules.name: The Dead-Zone Rule
rules.body: Social layer: no type in the IG UI dead zones, top ~170px and bottom ~280px on stories.

rules.name: The Flat-Plus-Scrim Rule
rules.body: Depth is a change of ground, not a stack of cards. Nested cards are always wrong.

rules.name: The No-Side-Stripe Rule
rules.body: A coloured border on one side of a card, callout or alert is banned outright.

rules.name: The Four-Field Rule
rules.body: Four required fields, and email is not one of them. A required free-text message is the heaviest thing you can put on a mobile form and is never required.

rules.name: The Calls-Are-The-Leads Rule
rules.body: On a phone-first page, tel: clicks are the primary conversion and the form submit is secondary. Track them that way or the ad platform optimises toward the weaker action.

dos: Do message-match the page headline to the ad that delivered the visitor. One h1, naming the service and the city.
Do give each service its own page and its own intent. Never point a hot water ad at a general electrician page.
Do strip the site navigation and unlink the wordmark on every ad landing page.
Do keep the form to four required fields, put it last, and label every input.
Do measure contrast rather than eyeballing it: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and for the border of any interactive control, checked on every surface the token touches.
Do clear 44px on every tap target, including phone numbers inside paragraphs and footers.
Do use real photography at a resized variant. A 1024px file at 80 to 160KB beats an 8MB original nobody waits for.
Do write alt text naming the actual project, not the category.
Do verify every image URL resolves before shipping.
Do ship pages with no JavaScript when the page doesn't need it.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion and hover:none on every transition.
donts: Don't put a tracked uppercase kicker above every section. On the web layer, don't use one at all.
Don't number sections unless the order is information the reader needs.
Don't use a coloured border on one side of anything.
Don't put an em dash in user-facing copy.
Don't require email, postcode, or a free-text message on a callback form.
Don't let a contrast fix on one surface go unchecked on the other surfaces that token appears on.
Don't put an unverified claim, price, rebate figure or review count on a client page.
Don't port one client's palette, voice or playbook onto another client's page.
Don't assume a page matches its spec because the spec was approved. Re-read the live markup after anyone else rebuilds it.
Don't add motion to an ad landing page for decoration. Motion competes with the conversion.
